chunks.arabic_text: ٢ - الْفَضْلُ بْنُ أَبِي قُرَّةَ، التَّمِيمِيُّ، السَّهْنَدِيُّ أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، آذَرْبَيْجَانِيٌّ، أَصْلُهُ كُوفِيٌّ، وَسَكَنَهَا. ضَعِيفٌ. وَمَا يَرْوِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: 2 – Al-Faḍl b. Abū Qurra, al-Tamīmī, al-Sahandī, Abū Muḥammad, Azerbaijani. His origin was Kufan, and he settled in it. Weak, and what he narrates from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* classifies Al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurra as a *thiqah* (reliable) yet slightly weak narrator (*da‘īf*) within the Shia tradition, specifically noting his transmission from Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS). His geographical roots in Kufa and later residence in Azerbaijan highlight the extensive network of Kufan scholars who disseminated hadith across the Islamic world. This classification is crucial for *rijāl* scholars assessing the authenticity of reports in the Four Books.
en.seo_question: Who is Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْفَضْلُ بْنُ أَبِي قُرَّةَ: Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, the narrator being evaluated
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator's reliability is questionable
key_terms.أَصْلُهُ كُوفِيٌّ: His origin was Kufan, referring to his ancestral home
key_terms.آذَرْبَيْجَانِيٌّ: Azerbaijani, indicating his residence or origin in that region
